description: Verify that after DHCPDECLINE the client waits at least 10 s before restarting configuration — DECLINE→DISCOVER #2 interval > (10 - ParamToleranceTime) s (RFC 2131 §3.1 SHOULD)
approach:
[Objective]
A tight loop of DECLINE → DISCOVER would hammer the server when many addresses are bad. RFC 2131 §3.1 says the client SHOULD pause at least 10 s before retrying.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DORA → BOUND → ARP Probe → conflict → DECLINE.
2. DUT → wire: DHCPDISCOVER #2 only after the wait.

[Pass condition]
(t_DISCOVER#2 - t_DECLINE) > (10 s - ParamToleranceTime).

[Fail condition]
Any chain step missing OR Fail_no_second_discover_in_window — DISCOVER #2 either absent OR arrived before the minimum wait elapsed.

verdicts.Pass: DUT paused ≥ 10 s after DECLINE before DISCOVER #2 — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_arp_probe: No DUT ARP Probe after BOUND
verdicts.Fail_no_decline: No DUT DHCPDECLINE after ARP conflict
verdicts.Fail_no_second_discover_in_window: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the DECLINE-to-DISCOVER window
